reasons: Lake identity gives case_name Pennsylvania v. Bruder, court U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided 1988-10-31, and year 1988.
Lake citations list official 488 U.S. 9, parallels 109 S. Ct. 205 and 102 L. Ed. 2d 172, and vendor_neutral 1988 U.S. LEXIS 4816.
Cached text header independently shows 488 U.S. 9 (1988), Supreme Court of United States, and Decided October 31, 1988.
The opinion describes a DUI traffic stop where Shallis administered field sobriety tests, asked Bruder to recite the alphabet, inquired about alcohol, then arrested him and gave Miranda warnings.

The opinion states that Berkemer held persons temporarily detained in ordinary traffic stops are not in custody for Miranda purposes and that the motorist was not entitled to warnings prior to arrest.
The opinion applies that rule to Bruder because the uncontested facts had the same noncoercive aspects as Berkemer and reverses the Superior Court's Miranda suppression ruling.
residual_risks: The holding must remain limited to ordinary traffic stops; the opinion expressly notes no absolute rule for all motorist detentions.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Preserve the ordinary/routine limitation and avoid implying coverage of prolonged or intimidating roadside detention.

reasons: The case directly concerns whether roadside questioning during an ordinary traffic stop was custodial interrogation requiring Miranda warnings.
The opinion repeatedly frames the controlling question as custody for Miranda purposes and applies Berkemer's ordinary-traffic-stop custody rule.
